reasoning: Recent coverage and polling in South Carolina over the last 45 days has focused almost entirely on the **Republican special Senate primary** following Lindsey Graham’s death, not on a general-election Senate or presidential matchup. Within that GOP primary, multiple reputable polls (Emerson College/Nexstar and Innovative Communication Strategies) consistently show Rep. Ralph Norman narrowly leading Sen. Darline Graham and other Republicans by low single digits, with very high undecided shares and margins within the error band, so the race is effectively an R vs. R toss-up rather than a D vs. R margin in a general election. Structurally, South Carolina remains a strongly Republican-leaning state (Cook PVI about R+8), and there are no new general-election presidential or Senate polls in the last 45 days that would justify stating a current D+/R+ margin for those contests specifically.

sources.name: The Hill summary of Emerson College/Nexstar South Carolina GOP Senate primary poll
sources.details: Emerson College Polling/Nexstar survey of 500 likely Republican voters in the South Carolina special GOP Senate primary found Ralph Norman at 22%, Darline Graham at 19%, Russell Fry at 12%, Mark Sanford at 11%, and about 25% undecided, with a 4.3-point margin of error, indicating Norman as a narrow frontrunner but the race still highly competitive.

sources.name: Nexstar/Emerson College South Carolina GOP Senate primary poll coverage
sources.details: A Nexstar/Emerson College Polling writeup similarly reports Norman leading with 22% to Graham’s 19% among likely Republican voters ahead of the August 11 special Senate primary, describing Norman as expected to come out on top in a tight race, again with no Democratic candidate tested in a general election matchup.

sources.name: WPDE coverage of Innovative Communication Strategies South Carolina GOP Senate primary poll
sources.details: An independent poll by Innovative Communication Strategies of 788 verified Republican primary voters found Ralph Norman at 18.6%, Darline Graham at 16.3%, Russell Fry at 11.7%, and 26.3% undecided, with Norman’s 2.3-point lead over Graham falling within the poll’s 3.5-point margin of error, indicating a statistically tied GOP primary field led nominally by Norman.

sources.details: Coverage of Jon Parker’s Innovative Communication Strategies poll in FITSNews similarly reports Norman leading the GOP Senate primary with 18.6% to Graham’s 16.3%, Fry at 11.7%, Lynch at 8.6%, and about 26.3% undecided, stressing that the race remains fluid despite Norman’s narrow advantage.
